MAJOR: Delta rows drained inside the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock are never digest-verified before the rename: `Swap` copies `id > lastID` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and commits immediately, so an id-reuse masked by ON CONFLICT or a divergent row in the delta bypasses the per-tenant count/SHA-256 comparison the AC requires "before the rename".

The out-of-range insert contract is broken: `audit_provision` raises `P0001` (plain RAISE EXCEPTION) for any month outside the 24-month/horizon window, so clients matching the AC-specified `23514` + stable message never see it; the only 23514 path (partition routing) is mostly preempted by the trigger.

AC deviation: `audit_late_YYYYMM` partitions ("strictly below grace, non-overlapping, cannot satisfy coverage") are not implemented; `audit_append_late` writes into canonical month partitions. The rationale is documented, but the AC and the coverage bullet are silently unmet — this needs an explicit AC/ADR amendment, not a comment.

AC gap: the "EDP service startup check" that must emit `audit_partition_months_ahead`/`audit_partition_low_coverage_total` non-fatally is absent from the diff; only the offline CLIs emit coverage, so a stale-coverage alert never fires in the running service.

TRUNCATE guard is inconsistent with its own comment ("owners ignore REVOKE: a statement trigger is the only guard"): statement triggers exist only on `audit_migration_state_events`/`audit_legal_hold_events`, while `audit_partitioned` and `audit_legal_hold_archive` rely on REVOKE, which the table owner bypasses — the live journal and hold archive remain owner-truncatable.

`VerifyHoldExtraction` digests use `string_agg(t::text, ...)`: record `::text` rendering depends on DateStyle/extra_float_digits/session settings, so the hold-archive vs live digest is not the reproducible, environment-independent SHA-256 the AC requires.
MINOR: `PurgeMonth` records `purged_at` before deleting cold objects; a mid-delete failure leaves a "purged" month with surviving objects and makes the hold guard emit a false spoliation rejection.
`RestoreMonth` leaves the `audit_restore_YYYYMM` scratch table and its `pf_runtime` SELECT grant behind indefinitely; no cleanup/teardown path exists.
0014 down drops most functions but orphans `audit_config_touch`, `audit_hold_guard`, `audit_deny_truncate` (and their definitions survive schema rollback).

`Down` copy-back uses a correlated `NOT EXISTS` against `audit_legacy` while holding ACCESS EXCLUSIVE — a seq scan on a large legacy table directly inflates the freeze window it is trying to keep short.

`edpdata.Append` classifies the heal case by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no partition of relation")` on top of SQLSTATE; message-text matching is locale/driver-fragile — prefer SQLSTATE 23514 plus the check-constraint name.
NIT: AC names the exhaustion signal `audit_swap_retry_exhausted`; the metric constant is `audit_swap_retry_exhausted_total` — confirm dashboards/alerts key off the implemented name.
`pfaudit-swap` uses package-level `activeMetrics`/`metricsEmitted` globals where a small struct would do.
`ExportMonth` re-reads the file twice (SHA-512... SHA-256 then Put) instead of Tee-ing during the initial read.
SUMMARY: Solid, unusually rigorous implementation: catalog-driven crash recovery, privilege-enforced hardening, separate advisory-lock namespaces, SSE-KMS fail-closed plumbing, and a genuinely destructive-test harness — the architecture direction is right.

Top risks are all integrity-boundary issues: the unverified delta drain under the swap lock, the broken 23514 out-of-range contract, the owner-bypassable TRUNCATE on the live journal/hold archive, and non-reproducible hold-archive digests.
One AC (audit_late partitions) and one AC (EDP startup coverage check) are effectively unimplemented and should be either delivered or formally amended before sign-off.
